newsitem.title: CHINA: China indicts six for rioting in Moslem region.
newsitem.headline: China indicts six for rioting in Moslem region.

text.p: China has indicted six people for their role in rioting in the western region of Xinjiang in February, a court official said on Thursday.

The official, speaking by telephone from Yining in the Moslem region of Xinjiang, said no one had been sentenced in the case and denied allegations by exiled separatists that two rioters would be executed on Thursday.
Uighur exiles in Kazakhstan's capital Almaty said on Wednesday that China planned to execute two religious students from the Moslem ethnic group on Thursday.
The exiles said the two men, Abu Khair and Abdu Medchit, both around 25 years old and religious students in Yining, would probably face a firing squad in the regional capital of Urumqi.
The Yining court official said the six people indicted in the case were charged with hooliganism and endangering social order.
The official declined to identify them, saying only they were all in their 30s and jobless, and that they would be sentenced next month.

In February, one of the largest demonstrations for independence in Xinjiang since the 1949 communist takeover turned violent, leaving nine people dead and 198 injured in Yining, near the region's border with Kazakhstan.
Xinjiang's capital of Urumqi was rocked the following month by a series of bus bombings that killed nine and wounded 74.

Exiled ethnic Uighurs, who want to set up an independent state of "East Turkestan" in Xinjiang, have claimed responsibility for the bombings and vowed to stage more attacks until they gain complete freedom for their homeland.
Chinese officials have said there was no evidence linking the unrest in Xinjiang to a bus bombing in Beijing this month.

But Beijing police have told hotels to strengthen security, and asked taxi drivers in the Chinese capital not to give rides to suspicious looking people from Xinjiang and to be especially cautious in neighbourhoods where many Uighur migrants live.

In a show of unity after the unrest, Chinese newspapers splashed on their front pages pictures of Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin wearing a traditional Uighur cap and shaking hands with a popular Uighur singer.
A controversial plan to move 50,000-100,000 people from the giant Three Gorges dam site to Xinjiang has been stalled by resistance from local authorities, Chinese sources have said.
Hans account for more than 90 percent of China's 1.2 billion people, but Xinjiang is populated mainly by Moslem, Turkic-speaking groups such as the Uighur ethnic minority.
Any plans to change the ethnic balance in Xinjiang would add to long-simmering tensions between Moslem ethnic groups and Han Chinese.
